c-sd-compare.label: Comparing surd expressions
c-sd-compare.summary: Square both sides (both positive) so the roots shrink, or compare decimals.

c-sd-conjugate.label: Conjugates and rationalising
c-sd-conjugate.summary: (a + √b)(a − √b) = a² − b removes the root. Pairs of conjugates often cancel to a clean number.

q-sd-compare.label: Which surd expression is greater?
q-sd-compare.summary: Sums of square roots on each side; decide <, > or =.

q-sd-rationalise.label: Rationalise and simplify
q-sd-rationalise.summary: Fractions with surds in the denominator, then an expression in x.

c-ix-indices.label: Laws of indices and equations in powers
c-ix-indices.summary: Write every base as a prime power, then add, subtract or multiply the exponents. Equal bases mean equal exponents.

c-ix-nested.label: Nested roots and infinite roots
c-ix-nested.summary: a + b ± 2√(ab) is a perfect square; an infinite root √(n + √(n + …)) is the positive root of x² = n + x.

c-ix-identity.label: Decimal sums that collapse by an identity
c-ix-identity.summary: Ugly decimals are a³ ± b³ over a² ∓ ab + b², or a perfect square. Spot the identity and the answer is a ± b.

q-ix-power.label: Evaluate an expression with fractional and negative powers

q-ix-eq.label: Find x (or n) from an equation in powers

q-ix-nested.label: Simplify a nested or infinite root

q-ix-identity.label: Collapse a decimal expression with an identity

q-sd-compare.cue: 'Which is greater?' with two sums of square roots.
q-sd-compare.eliminate: 'Cannot be determined' is almost never right when the numbers are all known. If one decimal sum is clearly larger, equality is out too.
traps: Comparing under the roots (5 + 7 against 12 + 3), which says equal.
Choosing 'cannot be determined' because the roots look awkward.

q-sd-rationalise.cue: A surd in a denominator, or x = (a + √b)/(a − √b) and a value of an expression in x.
q-sd-rationalise.standard: Multiply by the conjugate. For x = √((5 + 2√6)/(5 − 2√6)): the fraction equals (5 + 2√6)², so x = 5 + 2√6. Then x² + 3x − 15 = 49 + 20√6 + 15 + 6√6 − 15 = 49 + 26√6.
q-sd-rationalise.fast: Spot conjugate pairs: 1/(5 + √3) + 1/(5 − √3) = 10/(25 − 3), so the whole expression is 10/22 − 10/22 = 0.
q-sd-rationalise.eliminate: Compare the rational and root parts separately in the options (a + b√6): the √6 coefficient is 20 + 6 = 26, which singles out one option.
traps: Squaring (5 + 2√6) without the middle term: 25 + 24 instead of 49 + 20√6.
Forgetting the conjugate changes the sign inside only.
Adding fractions with different denominators without rationalising.

q-ix-power.cue: Fractional, decimal or negative powers of numbers like 16, 64, 243, 256.
q-ix-power.standard: Write each base as a prime power, add exponents of the same base: 243^0.16 × 243^0.04 = 243^0.2 = 3.
q-ix-power.fast: Add decimal exponents of the same base at once: 0.16 + 0.04 = 0.2, and 0.2 is the 5th root.
q-ix-power.eliminate: Check the sign and size: a negative exponent gives a number below 1 for a base above 1.
traps: Multiplying the exponents when the bases are multiplied (they are added).
Dropping the negative sign on a fractional power.
Taking a^(2/3) as the square root of a cube-root.

q-ix-eq.standard: Convert to the same base (27 = 3³), equate the exponents and solve the linear equation. For 3^x − 3^(x − 1): take out 3^(x − 1).
q-ix-eq.fast: Plug the options: for 3^(x − 1) = 243 only x = 6 works.
q-ix-eq.eliminate: Test the smallest option first: the powers grow quickly.
traps: Forgetting to multiply the exponent when converting 27^(2x + 1) = 3^(3(2x + 1)).

q-ix-nested.cue: Root inside a root, an endless √(n + √(n + …)), or a sum of such roots.
q-ix-nested.standard: Rewrite each inner root as (√a ± √b)²; for the infinite form solve x² = x + n and keep the positive root.
q-ix-nested.fast: Infinite root: split n into consecutive factors, 30 = 6 × 5, the answer is the larger one, 6. Or test each option.
q-ix-nested.eliminate: An infinite root is always larger than √n: √12 = 3.46 < x < 12.
traps: Taking the negative root of x² = x + n.
Splitting 11 + 2√30 as 5 + 6 but forgetting the product check (30).
Working from the outside of a nested root when the inside is a perfect square.

q-ix-identity.cue: Cubes and squares of ugly decimals, or numbers like 137, 133, 18221.
q-ix-identity.standard: Match the pattern: a³ − b³ over a² + ab + b² = a − b; a³ + b³ + c³ − 3abc over its partner = a + b + c. Read a and b from the numbers.
q-ix-identity.fast: Check if the odd-looking number is a product (137 × 133 = 18221, 0.0016 = 0.08 × 0.02): it is the ab term.
q-ix-identity.eliminate: The answer is a sum or difference of the numbers shown, so the magnitude fixes the option.
traps: Reading a² − ab + b² as a² + ab + b² and getting a + b instead of a − b.
Missing the extra 3abc in the a + b + c identity.
